en: The Legend of the Elder Suvaṇṇabibbohaniya The Chapter on the Golden Cradle, Number One [The Legend of the Elder Suvaṇṇabibbohaniya] In the past, during the time of the Buddha Kassapa, I was a wealthy merchant in Benares. Having heard that the Buddha had appeared in the world, I went to the Teacher and offered him a golden cradle. Because of that deed, for four incalculable eons And a hundred thousand aeons, I experienced the fruit of my merit. I was born in the realm of the Thirty-three, And there I enjoyed the five kinds of divine sensual pleasures. When the Blessed One attained parinirvāṇa, I was reborn in the city of Kusinārā. There, having heard that the Teacher had passed away, I went to the place where he lay between the twin sāla trees. I took a golden vessel and filled it with water, Then I poured it over the body of the Tathāgata. Because of that deed, I was reborn in heaven, And there I enjoyed the five kinds of divine sensual pleasures. After passing from that heavenly realm, I was reborn in the human world. In every birth, I was always wealthy, Possessing great power and abundant riches. Now, having heard that the Buddha has appeared in the world, I have come to pay homage to the Teacher. May the Blessed One accept this golden cradle; Through this gift, may I attain the goal of peace. The Blessed One accepted the offering, Out of compassion for me. By the power of that act of giving, I have now become an arahant. Thus did I perform a deed of merit in the past, Under the dispensation of the Buddha Kassapa. Through the ripening of that karma, I have now reached the end of suffering. This is the legend of the Elder Suvaṇṇabibbohaniya, The first in the Chapter on the Golden Cradle.
“With a mind full of faith, I gave him a single seat with my own hands,
and I also offered him a pillow for his feet.”
For the attainment of the supreme goal:
I do not recall ever being born in an unhappy state;
this is the fruit of that pillow.
a wheel-turning monarch endowed with the seven treasures and possessed of great power.
the six direct knowledges have been realized.
“Such is the teaching of the Buddha.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Suvaṇṇabibbohaniya recite these verses.
This is the first legend of the elder Suvaṇṇabibbohaniya.
